📸 Mañanera del Pueblo — Morelia, Michoacán · 3 de julio de 2026

🔥🇲🇽 Emilio Lozoya's sister arrested at Mexico City airport. The Agronitrogenados fraud case is still moving. "There is evidence of her participation in the fraud." — President Claudia Sheinbaum — Mañanera, July 3, 2026 Gilda Lozoya, sister of former Pemex director Emilio Lozoya, was detained on an outstanding arrest warrant tied to the Agronitrogenados case — the overpriced fertilizer-plant deal from the Peña Nieto years. García Harfuch stressed it followed a judicial order, not a political one. No impunity by surname.

🇲🇽🏭 Mexico is turning its avocado into protected national property: a Geographic Indication for 40,000 growers and 150,000 jobs. "The Geographic Indication of the Avocado adds value for more than 40,000 producers and more than 150,000 jobs." — Ximena Escobedo, Deputy Secretary — Mañanera, July 3, 2026 A Geographic Indication legally ties a product's name to its origin — the same tool that protects Champagne, Tequila and Colombian coffee. Applied to Michoacán's avocado, it keeps the value of a global export in the hands of the people who grow it. Economic sovereignty in practice.

🇲🇽⚖️ On USMCA: Mexico and Canada want the original terms respected. Only the US is trying to add new conditions. "The treaty stays in force for 10 years, and within those 10 years the decision can be made." — President Claudia Sheinbaum — Mañanera, July 3, 2026 Heading into the USMCA review, Sheinbaum said Mexico and Canada proposed keeping the treaty's original terms; Washington is the party pressing new conditions on rules of origin and import limits. The deal runs to 2036 with a possible extension — Mexico negotiates from certainty, not urgency.

🇲🇽🔍 Fighting extortion in Michoacán is the priority — and in practice that means protecting avocado and lime growers directly. "Direct protection for the productive sectors — especially avocado and lime growers, packers, traders and businesspeople." — Omar García Harfuch, Security Secretary — Mañanera, July 3, 2026 Extortion — the 'floor tax' that bled Michoacán's farmers for years — is the Plan Michoacán's stated target. Results so far: 1,300 arrests for high-impact crimes, 1,400 firearms and 215,000+ rounds seized, and over 35 tons of drugs.

🇲🇽🎨 21 Indigenous-language community houses. A P'urhépecha Linguistic Pride Network. That's what a "justice plan" looks like. "The National Institute of Indigenous Peoples has set up 21 Indigenous-Language Community Houses." — Violeta Vázquez-Rojas, Deputy Secretary of Science and Humanities — Mañanera, July 3, 2026 The P'urhépecha Justice Plan is one axis of Plan Michoacán. Alongside hospitals and roads, the state trained 25 linguistic promoters and launched a 'P'urhépecha Linguistic Pride Network.' Sheinbaum traveled to Cherán the same afternoon to lead it. Sovereignty starts with a people keeping its own language.

🇲🇽🔍 Homicides in Michoacán down 46%. June 2026 was the lowest month on record for the period. "There is a 46% decrease in the daily average of intentional homicide." — Marcela Figueroa, Executive Secretary, National Public Security System — Mañanera, July 3, 2026 Daily homicides fell from 4.32 (January 2025) to 2.33 (June 2026) — a 37% year-on-year drop. Michoacán was the first state Felipe Calderón militarized in December 2006, launching the 'war on drugs.' The strategy that replaced it is delivering the numbers the war never did.

🇲🇽✊ Mexico's security doctrine in one line: it's built on justice and rights, not war. "Security is sustained by strategy, action and justice — guaranteeing the people's rights to education, health, housing and dignified work. Development with justice and wellbeing." — Rosa Icela Rodríguez, Interior Secretary — Mañanera, July 3, 2026, Morelia Presenting the 12-axis Plan Michoacán, the government framed public safety as guaranteed rights, not militarization. Michoacán — the first state Calderón militarized in December 2006 to launch the 'war on drugs' — is now the test case for the opposite approach.
